The racers gradually draw closer to the truth.
But humanity doesn’t even know who the real enemy is.

In such a world—
Can we survive to the very end?

126103.synopsis:
Ji Weiyi — film industry investor, group’s beloved rich second-generation, born with a hole in his heart and almost didn’t live to adulthood.
His family has only one expectation for him: just don’t die.
A fortune teller once told him that the age of 32 would be a dangerous hurdle, one only solvable if he meets his Tianyi Nobleman (a savior figure).
At 32, Ji Weiyi returns to his hometown for a funeral and sees Zhang Yuan fishing by the river—a half-worn hearing aid hanging from his neck, pitch-black pupils like a stray dog.
Ji Weiyi’s heart skipped a beat—not that kind of heart flutter.
It’s just that the art-house film he’s investing in happens to be missing a novice male lead.
So Ji Weiyi takes Zhang Yuan back to Beijing and pushes him into his home.
Zhang Yuan, who had spent his first 18 years in isolation, with poor hearing and few words, turns out to be like a personal ironclad bodyguard—
He massages Ji Weiyi’s head when it hurts, keeps his stomach warm when it aches, and watches movies with him when he can’t sleep.
Even when Ji Weiyi has a heart attack…
Ji Weiyi: “Just call 120 (emergency services), no need to give me artificial respiration.”
To Ji Weiyi, Zhang Yuan is still just a kid, innocent and clueless, and he doesn’t want to scare him.
So when Zhang Yuan keeps staring at his lips, Ji Weiyi assumes he’s reading them.
When Zhang Yuan comes into his bedroom on rainy nights, Ji Weiyi thinks he’s afraid of thunder.
When Zhang Yuan rests his head on his chest to listen to his heartbeat, Ji Weiyi can’t bring himself to refuse.
He even lets him listen and reassures him:
“It’s okay, I can still breathe. I’m not going to die.”
One day, Zhang Yuan asks, “Someone said… you’re my sugar daddy?”
Ji Weiyi: “No, I’m what you call Party A (the client).”
Privately fuming, wondering who’s been filling Zhang Yuan’s head with nonsense.
The kid is still young—easy to fool.
Until later—
Sweat drips from the tip of Zhang Yuan’s nose onto Ji Weiyi’s face.
Ji Weiyi calls his name in broken, incoherent gasps…and in his daze, he can’t help but think, Who’s the one being fooled here, really?!

earning a formidable reputation as a highly skilled investigator.
